message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to make live calls to external services like VirusTotal. However, here’s how you could retrieve the information you’re looking for using the VirusTotal API:

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/relationships/subdomains?limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc" \
  -H "x-apikey: my_api"
```

The response will contain a list of related objects. To keep only the IDs and any context attributes, you can filter the JSON like this (using `jq` as an example):

```bash
curl ... | jq '.data[] | {id: .id, context_attributes: .context_attributes}'
```

If you prefer to do it programmatically in Python:

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/relationships/subdomains"
headers = {"x-apikey": "my_api"}
params = {"limit": 10, "continuation_cursor": "abc"}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
resp.raise_for_status()
results = resp.json()

# Extract only IDs and context attributes
filtered = [
    {"id": item["id"], "context_attributes": item.get("context_attributes")}
    for item in results.get("data", [])
]

print(filtered)
```

Replace `"my_api"` with your actual API key. This will give you a list of subdomain object IDs along with any context attributes that VirusTotal returns.
